description.to:
As an optimization operator, I want required semantic-evidence access failures to be identified before model-backed diagnosis and explained plainly, so that a credential problem is never reported as an unexplained incomplete score diagnosis.

Feature: Semantic evidence prerequisite failures

Scenario: Required rubric evidence cannot be read
  Given a portfolio run can read production records through the application API
  But its worker cannot read a required rubric-evidence source
  When semantic diagnosis preflight runs
  Then the run records a typed required-evidence failure
  And it does not spend semantic-model budget for that target
  And it does not launch an optimizer for that target
  And the living Report names the unavailable evidence category and a safe operator next action

Scenario: Failure details are safe
  Given a required evidence read fails with provider-specific details
  When the failure is published to stakeholder and operator views
  Then the stakeholder view uses a concise sanitized explanation
  And restricted evidence preserves the failure class without exposing credentials, object keys, raw content, or secrets

Scenario: Evidence access is healthy
  Given all required evidence sources pass preflight
  When semantic diagnosis begins
  Then the existing diagnosis, budget, and automatic-execution policies continue unchanged

Out of scope: new GraphQL resources, schema changes, automatic promotion, guideline edits, feedback-setting changes, and client-specific data.
